candidates.title: Put the most relevant retrieved document first (or last), not mid-context
candidates.rule: When building a retrieval-augmented prompt with many documents, rank/rerank so the most likely answer-bearing passage sits at the very start (or very end) of the context rather than in the middle.
candidates.passage: models are often much better at using relevant information that occurs at the very beginning (primacy bias) and very end of contexts
candidates.finding: Across 10/20/30-document NaturalQuestions-Open settings, accuracy forms a U-shape with gold-document position; e.g. GPT-3.5-Turbo with 20 docs scored 75.8% at index 0, 53.8% at index 9, 63.2% at index 19. Worst-case mid-context accuracy fell below closed-book (56.1%). The authors suggest reranking as a remedy but did not implement a reranking pipeline, so the ordering prescription is an extrapolation from the position-sweep results.
workloads: Multi-document QA built from NaturalQuestions-Open with Contriever-retrieved distractors
Synthetic JSON key-value retrieval with UUIDs
candidates.conditions: Exactly one gold document among k-1 retrieved distractors; greedy decoding; accuracy = answer string appears in output; contexts of ~1.5K-5K tokens for QA. Trend held with random distractors and randomized distractor order.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, 2023-era models; no end-to-end reranker was evaluated, so gains from reordering are inferred. Magnitude varies by model (Claude-1.3 is flatter than GPT-3.5-Turbo) and could differ for newer long-context models.
candidates.validation_test: In your RAG stack, hold retrieval fixed and compare answer accuracy when the top-ranked passage is placed first versus in the middle of the context, across your own query set.

candidates.title: Repeat the query after the documents for exact-match retrieval, but don't expect it to fix QA
candidates.rule: For decoder-only models doing exact-token lookup over structured context, place the query both before and after the data; do not assume the same trick improves open-ended multi-document QA.
candidates.passage: query-aware contextualization dramatically improves performance on the key-value retrieval task—all models achieve near-perfect performance on the 75, 140, and 300 key-value pair settings
candidates.finding: Placing the key before and after the JSON object lifted GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) from a 45.6% worst-case at 300 pairs to perfect accuracy. The same change had only marginal effects on multi-document QA: slightly better when the gold doc was first, slightly worse elsewhere — a reported null result.
candidates.conditions: Decoder-only models that cannot attend to a trailing query while encoding earlier tokens; query duplication costs a small number of extra tokens.
candidates.limitations: Benefit demonstrated only on a synthetic exact-match task with no natural-language semantics; explicitly did not transfer to QA. 2023 model versions; unclear for newer models or longer natural-language contexts.
candidates.validation_test: Run your lookup-style task with the query only after the data versus duplicated before and after, measuring accuracy by position of the target item.

candidates.title: Stop adding retrieved documents once reader accuracy saturates
candidates.rule: In retriever-reader setups, tune the number of retrieved documents on reader accuracy rather than retriever recall; past roughly 20 passages extra context mostly buys latency and cost.
candidates.passage: Using more than 20 retrieved documents only marginally improves reader performance ( ∼ 1.5% for GPT-3.5-Turbo and ∼ 1% for Claude-1.3)
candidates.finding: On NaturalQuestions-Open with Contriever+MS-MARCO retrieval, retriever recall kept rising while reader accuracy plateaued, so additional documents mainly increased input length, latency and cost.
workloads: Open-domain QA on NaturalQuestions-Open (paragraph-answer subset) with Contriever retrieval over Wikipedia
candidates.conditions: Standard retriever-reader prompt that concatenates retrieved passages; accuracy judged by answer string match.
candidates.limitations: The 20-document threshold is dataset-, retriever- and model-specific; the authors note the trade-off is task-specific. Only two closed models measured; no cost figures given beyond qualitative latency/cost claims.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep k (e.g. 5/10/20/50) on your own queries, plotting retriever recall and end answer accuracy plus latency and token cost, and pick the knee of the accuracy curve.

reason: The paper runs controlled position/length experiments on multi-document QA, synthetic key-value retrieval, and a retriever-reader case study, yielding several scoped, actionable prompt-construction rules with explicit null results.
